name: Transcribe an audio file
notes: File in, file out: one audio.transcribe step. The transcript is written atomically to <output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json (schema 1: audio_sha256, model, language, duration, segments [{start, end, text}], created_at, window_count, empty_window_count); the outputs carry only scalars, never the text. Re-running the same audio and model is a no-op; another model writes a second file beside the first. The workflow knows nothing about where the file came from.

steps.name: Transcribe the file
steps.notes: audio.transcribe through stt-en. Checks audio_sha256 (64 hex), keeps audio_path under the actor's audio_root and output_dir under its output_root (path_refused), hashes the file (audio_mismatch), and returns the existing <output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json unchanged when its audio_sha256 and model match (no request). Otherwise ffmpeg cuts 16 kHz mono WAV windows of at most 480 s (at a silence in a window's last 60 s when there is one), each POSTed to <base_url>/v1/audio/transcriptions; each reply is kept under .work.<model-slug>/ so a retry resends only the missing windows. timeout_s 14400 covers a 3.8 h recording (the engine default is 3600 s); only stt_unavailable is retried.
